title: onprem-legal-ops-risk-qa-and-stakeholder-scripts
body:
Purpose and scope:
This brief is a pragmatic field playbook for sales, solutions, and legal ops when pursuing regulated buyers who require private (VPC / on-prem) deployment options. It focuses on: control plane terminology customers understand, pre-baked contract language we can offer, common procurement/legal redlines and suggested concessions, and short scripts for seller/SEs when answering sensitive questions from CISOs, procurement, and legal teams.

Why this exists (why different from existing materials):
- Most existing materials assume the conversation starts with security architecture. This doc starts with contracting and procurement realities — the questions and asks that block deals late in the cycle.
- Combines realistic legal language candidates with tactical negotiation trade-offs and stakeholder-specific messaging.

Top-level narrative (1-min seller script):
"Redwood’s Private deployment gives your engineering team the performance and lifecycle control of our hosted stack while keeping your data and control plane inside your environment. We operate a lightweight customer-managed control plane — you own the network, KMS, and audit trail; we provide versioned runtime images, automated upgrades, and an SLA for management services. We only request the minimal administrative access needed to deliver updates and telemetry, and we offer options for air-gapped installs and in-country hosting to meet regulatory constraints."

Control plane language — friendly, procurement-safe variants:
- Customer-managed control plane (preferred): "Customer retains ownership of the control plane, hosts it in their VPC, and controls network and keying. Redwood provides signed deployment artifacts, upgrade tooling, and optional support connectors."
- Hosted control plane with customer network controls (alternate): "Redwood operates the control plane but encrypts and restricts control plane API access to customer-managed endpoints and enforces customer KMS for secrets."
- Air-gapped on-prem package (compliance option): "Fully offline install bundle plus validated installation runbook and periodic signed releases."

Contract clauses to pre-seed (language we can offer internally):
- Data residency: "Customer Data shall at all times remain in the Customer Environment and not be exported from the specified region without Customer consent."
- Access & admin: "Redwood personnel will only be granted access by an explicit, auditable request from Customer admins for specific tasks. All access requests are scoped, time-limited, and logged."
- Audit rights narrow scope: "Customer audit rights are limited to verification of environment configuration and Redwood-provided logs; no right to access Redwood internal logs or source code."
- SLA for managed services: "Redwood guarantees X% availability of management operations (installer, upgrade coordination, support portal responses) and provides rollback/restore assistance during failed updates."
- Indemnity & liability carveouts: "Mutual indemnities for third-party IP only; limitation of liability aligns with ARR tiers and excludes consequential damages; security incidents caused by Customer-controlled misconfiguration are excluded."

Common procurement/legal redlines and suggested responses:
- Redline: "We need full source code escrow."
  - Response: Offer periodic delivery of signed binaries, detailed runbooks, and an optional escrow for critical components at enterprise commitment levels; explain maintenance burden and propose escrow with release triggers tied to specific events.
- Redline: "Unlimited audit rights and access to logs."
  - Response: Offer on-site audit or SOC2/HIPAA report sharing under NDA and limited access to operational logs; narrow scope to Redwood-managed artifacts.
- Redline: "Broad indemnity for any data loss."
  - Response: Propose mutual indemnity and carve out incidents caused by Customer negligence or misconfiguration; propose insurance-backed cap.
- Redline: "We require complete control plane isolation with no external calls."
  - Response: Offer air-gapped installation option and signed offline installers with documented update process; if telemetry is required for support, provide opt-in secure channels or physical upload procedures.

Concession matrix (what we can flex vs what we should not):
- Flexible: telemetry granularity (we can accept turn-off of non-essential telemetry), maintenance windows, limited escrow opt-in, extra onboarding support hours
- Hard/anchor: ability to deliver signed binaries/upgrade images, indemnity caps tied to ARR, status of access controls (must be auditable/time-limited), and we cannot open-source core proprietary runtime.

Checklist of artifacts to prepare for procurement/legal meetings:
- SOC2 Type II / ISO attestation PDFs (or equivalent), redacted if needed
- Copies of our default private deployment contract template (highlighted clauses)
- Runbook: install, upgrade, rollback steps (pdf)
- KMS integration guide and key handoff procedures
- Audit log schema + sample logs (redacted)
- Support/escrow options and pricing sheet
- Network topology diagram showing minimal ports and control-plane endpoints

Stakeholder-focused micro-scripts (one-liners and short walkthroughs):
- CISO (security first): "You keep the keys, we only deliver signed artifacts and an ops interface. We can demonstrate SOC2 mapping to your controls and show a plan for isolation and emergency rollback."
- Head of Procurement: "We understand standard redlines; here are three options — self-managed control plane with standard SLA, hosted-but-KMS-managed, or air-gap with an enterprise onboarding retainer."
- CTO/Platform lead: "Your team retains full lifecycle control and can pin runtime versions. Redwood supplies automation and a validated upgrade path so you don’t take on long-term maintenance burden."
- Legal: "We’ll accept a scoped audit clause and provide a technical escrow option for enterprise commitments; we propose mutual indemnities and a negotiated cap tied to fees paid."

Competitive callouts (how to position vs typical alternatives):
- Versus hyperscalers (managed endpoints): emphasize control plane ownership and clear artifact signing, explain that hyperscalers often leave ambiguity around telemetry and cross-tenant routing; we sell predictable economics and portability.
- Versus self-built inference stacks: emphasize our runtime optimizations, security hardening, and maintenance SLAs — lower total cost of ownership and faster time-to-pilot.
- Versus pure on-prem vendors: highlight our hybrid options (air-gap plus managed tooling) and product roadmap for quantization/throughput improvements; we offer modern SaaS-style lifecycle without sacrificing isolation.

Negotiation play examples (short role-play templates):
- Scenario: CISO asks for unlimited audit + source code escrow
  - Seller: "We hear you — audits validate compliance, escrow protects long-term availability. For most customers we provide SOC2 + onsite audit. For source code escrow we can include signed binaries and a targeted escrow for the management plane at enterprise tiers; let’s scope triggers so it’s actionable and affordable."
- Scenario: Procurement wants huge indemnity and low liability cap
  - Seller: "We propose a mutual indemnity with an ARR-proportional cap and propose cloud-security exceptions for customer misconfigurations; we can include cyber-insurance confirmation if helpful."

Quick rebuttals to late-stage objections:
- Objection: "We can’t allow any external control plane calls."
  - Rebuttal: "We offer a fully air-gapped distribution and verified offline upgrade path; if you need ongoing support we can agree to secure, customer-initiated data pulls only."
- Objection: "We need direct access to vendor logs during incident response."
  - Rebuttal: "We’ll provide redacted operational timelines and a joint incident response runbook that ensures you get actionable evidence without exposing internal vendor telemetry."

Next steps for field team (practical ops):
1) Attach this playbook to the deal record and add SOC2/ISO artifacts to the data room.
2) Run a 30-minute pre-call with Legal Ops + Solutions Engineer to pre-seed the customer’s redlines.
3) Offer the customer a 2-week technical POC with a clearly defined scope and rollback criteria; include a contract addendum limiting audit scope during POC.
4) If the buyer insists on escrow/source code, escalate to Product + Legal for a scoped enterprise offer and price uplift.

Appendix — short templated email for procurement: 
Subject: Redwood Private deployment: proposed contract options and compliance artifacts
Hi <Procurement lead>,

Thanks for the conversation today — attached are the proposed contract options we discussed (self-managed control plane, hosted-with-KMS, and air-gapped). Also attached: SOC2 report, install runbook, and a compact list of concession options. Happy to jump on a call with Legal Ops to walk through redlines and propose an enterprise escrow option if helpful.

Best,
Asha

---
Editor notes: This doc is draft and intended as a living playbook. Next review 2025-02-01. Additions requested: sample install runbook export, legal-approved escrow language, and a one-pager for customer security champions.
